I did make a fix using ps and grep as alternatives.

(If anyone is unfamiliar with ssh-agent, it caches credentials for use with ssh. If you have a password-protected rsa key that you use for a server, you can store the key in ssh-agent with ssh-add, allowing you to only use the password once. It automatically works with ssh for the rest of your session provided that the proper environment variables are set, which is printed out by ssh-agent when it is spawned. ssh-agent is provided with openssh.)
